rules.source_section: Stroke and Vascular Disease / Evaluation of Known or Suspected Stroke (11,12)
rules.source_quote: Evaluation of Known or Suspected Stroke (11,12)

criteria.description: Known or clinically suspected acute ischemic stroke or intracranial hemorrhage

required_documentation: Emergency medical records documenting focal neurologic deficit, NIH Stroke Scale, or last known normal time
rules.review_notes: Emergency stroke evaluation pathway for non-contrast brain CT.

rules.source_section: Evaluation of Known or Suspected Vascular Disease (13)
rules.source_quote: Evaluation of suspected acute subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH)

criteria.description: Clinical suspicion of acute subarachnoid hemorrhage

required_documentation: Clinical notes documenting sudden onset severe thunderclap headache or signs of meningismus
rules.review_notes: Urgent non-contrast CT for acute subarachnoid hemorrhage.

rules.source_section: INDICATIONS / Head Trauma / Evaluation of Known or Suspected Trauma (14,15)
rules.source_quote: Known or suspected trauma or injury to the head with documentation of one or more of

criteria.description: Known or suspected acute head trauma with acute, new, or fluctuating focal neurologic findings, motor changes, or mental status changes

required_documentation: Emergency department notes or trauma physical examination documenting mechanism of head injury and acute neurological deficits
rules.review_notes: Brain CT is the primary modality for acute head trauma evaluation.

rules.source_section: INDICATIONS / Evaluation of Headache (1,2) / Acute, sudden onset headache
rules.source_quote: Acute, sudden onset headache (< 4 weeks), with any ONE of the following

criteria.description: Acute sudden onset severe headache presenting within 48 hours of onset ('worst headache of life' or 'thunderclap' headache) concerning for acute subarachnoid hemorrhage

required_documentation: Clinical notes documenting acute peak headache onset within seconds to minutes and physical examination
rules.review_notes: Non-contrast Brain CT is initial test of choice for acute sudden severe headache / suspected SAH.
